persona.title: Pretend you are…
persona.text: Pretend you are Brian, 17, in Kisii. Your grandmother, Kwamboka, is 70 and just got her first smartphone. She keeps hearing about 'AI' on the radio, and last week someone sent her a message asking for money, so she is worried about scams. Today you sit with her and go through the AI course together, one lesson at a time.

lines: Welcome. This short video explains an app called Daraja Academy. You have never seen it before, and that is fine.

First, the problem. Many older people hear about AI every day. AI means artificial intelligence: computer programs like ChatGPT or Claude that can answer questions and write text, the way a person would.
Young people learn these tools quickly. But many grandparents feel left behind, or afraid. They also face new scams. A cheat can now copy a voice or a face, and send messages that look real.
Daraja Academy is a short course called AI for Grandparents. It has six lessons of about ten minutes each. Each lesson uses big words, one idea at a time, and nothing you do can break anything.

Who uses it? Older people, often with a grandchild next to them. The course was made in America, so some examples are American, like Netflix, a film company, or gift cards. The lessons fit every family.
Let us look at the course home page.

lines.t: At the top is a green note. This is your teacher. The first time, it asks your first name. Type the name and tap That's me.
Under the teacher is a bar. It shows how many of the six lessons are finished.

Then come the lesson cards. Each card shows the lesson number, its name and the minutes. Lesson 1 is Just ask it. Lesson 2 is Spot the fake. Lesson 5 is Let it write with you. Tap a card to open that lesson.
At the bottom is a wide card for the diploma, a certificate. It opens when all six lessons are finished.

lines: The price shows in dollars, but while we are testing, all six lessons are open and free.
Now, inside a lesson. Each page has one idea. The dots at the top show how far you are. The button Read this page to me reads the page out loud.
At the bottom of each page, the green button goes forward. It says Next, or something like I'm ready. The white button goes back.
Some pages let you practise. In lesson 1 there is a safe practice AI inside the lesson. You tap a question, and its answer appears below.
Then a page called Now ask something real. You type your own question in the box. For the test you only need to type it; you do not need to open ChatGPT.
In lesson 2, Spot the fake, five messages appear one by one. For each one you tap Fake or Real, and the app tells you why. Then tap Next one.
In lesson 5, Let it write with you, you build a request by tapping three things: who it is to, what it is for, and how it should sound. The request writes itself at the bottom.

Every lesson ends with a one question quiz. Tap A, B or C. Green shows the right answer. Then tap Finish the lesson. The last page says Lesson done. Only then is the lesson counted as finished, with a tick on its card.
If you stop in the middle, the app opens on the same page next time.
To start again with an empty course, scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap Start fresh, erase this app's data. The app asks twice before it erases anything.
In the test, you will be a grandchild doing lessons with your grandmother. Take your time. If something is confusing, say so. That is exactly what we want to find.

challenge.intro: Now you are Brian, sitting with your grandmother Kwamboka. The course is empty. Nobody will tell you which button to press. Use what you learned. If the teacher asks for a name, you can type Kwamboka. When you finish, tap Check my work.
challenge.start: Open Daraja Academy with the normal link (not the 🧪 test copy). If the welcome tour shows, tap 'skip the tour' → '✨ Start fresh with my own' → OK. If a menu asking 'What would you like to do?' covers the page, tap '↩ Pick up where I left off' first. Then scroll to the very bottom of the page and tap '🧹 Start fresh — erase this app’s data' → OK → OK. The bar says '0 of 6 lessons done' and no card has a ✅. (Verified 10 Oct: all five checks false after this.)

tasks.text: Finish lesson 1 with your grandmother, all the way to the end, including its quiz.
tasks.hint: A lesson only counts when you reach its last page, after the quiz. Look for a ✅ on the lesson 1 card.

tasks.text: Cucu wants to know how to keep sukuma wiki fresh for three days without a fridge. In lesson 1, put her real question where the lesson asks for one.
tasks.hint: Lesson 1 has a page called 'Now ask something REAL'. Type her question in the box there. You do not need to open ChatGPT.

tasks.text: Your grandmother is afraid of scams. Finish the lesson that teaches how to spot a fake message.
tasks.hint: Lesson 2 is 'Spot the fake'. Answer all five messages, then the quiz, then reach the last page.

tasks.text: Cucu wants AI to help her write a funny birthday note to her granddaughter. Build that request in the lesson about writing.
tasks.hint: Lesson 5, 'Let it write with you', has a page where you tap who it is to, what it is for, and how it should sound.

tasks.text: Finish that writing lesson, all the way to the end.
tasks.hint: Keep tapping the green button through lesson 5, answer its quiz, and reach the page that says Lesson 5 done.

ownWords.question: In your own words, what is this app for?
keyIdeas: a short course that teaches older people to use AI
how to ask AI questions and let it help you write
how to spot fakes and scams and check answers

daily.task: Do one more part of a lesson in Daraja Academy, or answer one quiz question.
